angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 79,309,800 km at 1125.90 pc = 0.94 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Groenewegen (2013), A&A 550, A70, table10, T Mon: Baade-Wesselink distance (pc) 1125.9 +/- 33 (Monte-Carlo) (https://arxiv.org/abs/1212.5478): 1125.9 +/- 33 pc; Gaia DR3 parallax 0.7141 +/- 0.0517 mas (same row, RUWE 1.72), 13.8 standard errors, is not used
radiusSource: Radius 114 +/- 3.4 solar radii from Groenewegen (2013), A&A 550, A70, table10, T Mon: Baade-Wesselink mean radius (solar radii) 114 +/- 3.4 (Monte-Carlo) (https://arxiv.org/abs/1212.5478): 79,309,800 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. No mass is measured, so GM is 0, the records' unpublished value. Temperature 4875 +/- 189 K from Groenewegen (2020), A&A 635, A33, VizieR J/A+A/635/A33/table1, recno 175, Name='T Mon', columns Teff, e_Teff (K): Teff 4875 +/- 189 K from a fit to the spectral energy distribution at mean light (not spectroscopic) (https://arxiv.org/abs/2002.02186). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Groenewegen (2020), A&A 635, A33, VizieR J/A+A/635/A33/table1, recno 175, Name='T Mon', columns Teff, e_Teff (K): Teff 4875 +/- 189 K from a fit to the spectral energy distribution at mean light (not spectroscopic) (https://arxiv.org/abs/2002.02186)
surfaceGravitySource: log g 0.49 from 2024A&A...690A.246T; the 21 published values span log g 0.49 to 1.46, across which the limb law changes by at most 1.4% of the centre brightness (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A%26A...690A.246T)
spectralTypeSource: SIMBAD, V* T Mon: spectral type G3Iabv+A0p (2013AJ....146...93E)
projectedRotationSpeedSource: SIMBAD, V* T Mon: projected rotation speed 20 km/s, the measurement SIMBAD prefers (2005yCat.3244....0G)

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from a blackbody at the star's published temperature (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
